children: British digital bank Revolut has applied for a Swiss banking licence and unveiled plans to invest more than 150 million Swiss francs ($183 million) to expand in the lucrative Swiss market.
The company has applied for a licence with the Financial Market Supervisory Authority (Finma), Revolut said on Wednesday.
Approval would allow Revolut to offer customers in Switzerland a broader range of services, including salary accounts, access to Swiss deposit insurance, and local IBAN account numbers.
It would make Revolut's Swiss business the fourth standalone bank it operates in Europe, after Britain, Lithuania, and France, said Chief Commercial Officer David Tirado.
"This reflects the importance we give to this market," he told Reuters.
Until now, the fintech has been limited in Switzerland by the fact that it cannot offer salary accounts or investment accounts denominated in francs.
"In Switzerland, we have 1.3 million customers, which corresponds to a penetration of around 24%," said Tirado. "In two to three years, we would expect to surpass 40%."
The application is part of the company's expansion strategy.
Earlier this month, Revolut received preliminary approval for a national banking licence in the United States. It secured banking licences in Britain and France earlier this year.
Currently, Revolut operates in Switzerland and Germany through Revolut Bank UAB, which is licensed in Lithuania.
"What we are currently missing to compete with incumbent Swiss banks is trust," said Tirado. "We think this is the missing piece of the puzzle."
Over the next five years, Revolut also plans to invest more than 150 million francs in Switzerland.
The workforce, currently around 30 employees, will be tripled by the end of next year, said Switzerland general manager Julian Biegmann.
"We'll build out our local team significantly, all the functions you need to have in order to operate as a Swiss bank," he said.
